boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, walkable destinations on corridors linking the University of Arkansas with Fayetteville’s downtown.

cards.title: ArtCourt
cards.subtitle: Dickson Street corridor
cards.notes: Bring a basketball if you want to play; the outdoor art-and-basketball space is first come, first served on West Dickson Street.
cards.short_summary: A public court where murals, lighting, and play share one compact outdoor space.
cards.evidence_claim: ArtCourt at 227 W. Dickson St. is open to spontaneous visitors, is first come first served, and has free entry.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 9:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m.; hours can change for weather or maintenance. Bring your own ball.

cards.title: Walton Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Dickson Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the current performance calendar, then use the front-of-house setting as a clear landmark while moving between campus and downtown.
cards.short_summary: A major Fayetteville performing-arts venue directly on Dickson Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Walton Arts Center is located on Dickson Street in Fayetteville.
cards.source_title: I’m Going to Walton Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Performance access and ticket requirements vary by event; consult the venue calendar before visiting.

cards.title: Dickson St. Bookshop
cards.subtitle: Dickson Street corridor
cards.notes: Browse the used and out-of-print shelves at 325 West Dickson; allow time to look through the broad subject sections.
cards.short_summary: An independent bookshop with more than 100,000 used and out-of-print books.
cards.evidence_claim: Dickson St. Bookshop is at 325 West Dickson Street and states that it has over 100,000 used and out-of-print books.
cards.access_notes: The shop lists daily hours; confirm them on its website before making a special trip.

cards.title: TheatreSquared
cards.subtitle: West Avenue corridor, one block south of Dickson Street
cards.notes: Look for the theatre at the West Avenue end of the Dickson area and check its season page for productions and event details.
cards.short_summary: A professional regional-theatre destination at the downtown end of the campus-to-Dickson walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Fayetteville identifies TheatreSquared as one of the performing-arts destinations in the Dickson Street area.
cards.access_notes: Show access, times, and ticket requirements depend on the selected production.

cards.title: Upper Ramble
cards.subtitle: Dickson Street and West Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Pause at the plaza’s swings, water feature, playable art, lawn, and picnic area before continuing toward the downtown core.
cards.short_summary: A public linear-park plaza that starts at Dickson Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Upper Ramble at Dickson and West includes a shade structure with swings, a granite water feature, playable art, lawn, and picnic area.
cards.source_title: Visit a Fayetteville Attraction this Summer!
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public space; event programming and conditions can affect how areas are used.

cards.title: Fayetteville Town Center
cards.subtitle: West Mountain Street and Block Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the Town Center plaza as a downtown waypoint, then continue along Block Avenue toward the Square and its public-facing events.
cards.short_summary: A downtown event venue beside the Block Avenue approach to the Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Fayetteville identifies Fayetteville Town Center as a downtown community venue and places it near the Dickson and Square district.
cards.source_title: Fun Places to Stay on Dickson Street
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on scheduled events and the venue’s operating arrangements.

cards.title: Fayetteville Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: Block Avenue corridor at the Downtown Square
cards.notes: Plan around the published market day, start at the Square, and use the vendor map if you want to locate a particular producer.
cards.short_summary: A year-round market of locally grown and made goods on the Downtown Square.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fayetteville Farmers Market operates year round and offers locally grown and locally made goods; Saturday markets are on the Downtown Square.
cards.access_notes: Market schedules vary by season; the market’s FAQ publishes current days and times. Purchases are optional.

cards.title: Fayetteville Public Library
cards.subtitle: School Avenue corridor near West Mountain Street
cards.notes: Use the library as an indoor downtown stop, and check its calendar or service desk information before planning a program visit.
cards.short_summary: A named civic destination on the School Avenue side of downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fayetteville Farmers Market directs online-order customers to pick up at the Fayetteville Public Library’s South Parking Lot on School Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Library services and program access may have separate schedules; verify details with the library before visiting.

cards.title: Old Main
cards.subtitle: Arkansas Avenue corridor at the University of Arkansas edge
cards.notes: Approach along Arkansas Avenue to view the university’s signature historic building, then continue downhill toward the Dickson Street corridor.
cards.short_summary: A named University of Arkansas landmark at the campus edge closest to downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Fayetteville describes the Inn at Carnall Hall as having a porch view of Old Main and being steps from Dickson Street.
cards.source_title: Fun Places to Stay on Dickson Street
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is appropriate for a walk-through; building access can vary with university operations.

cards.title: Inn at Carnall Hall
cards.subtitle: West Avenue corridor beside the Dickson Street approach
cards.notes: Use the 1905 former women’s dormitory as a historic campus-edge landmark while walking between Old Main and the Dickson area.
cards.short_summary: A preserved 1905 campus building on the short walk between Old Main and downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Fayetteville states that Inn at Carnall Hall was built in 1905 as a women’s dormitory and is steps from Dickson Street.
cards.source_title: Fun Places to Stay on Dickson Street
cards.access_notes: The building also operates as an inn; respect guest areas and verify access for any services or dining.
